title: Differentially Private Geodesic Regression
claim: Privacy error depends strongly on how the budget is split between parameters and shrinks as sample size grows.
layout: 2 stacked line plots sharing y-label; budget-split annotations at each point
description: Two vertically stacked line plots, both with log energy (log average MSE) on the y-axis and an index from 0 to 9 on the x-axis. Each plot has three coloured lines with dots: blue for 20 data points, orange for 50, and green for 100. Dashed horizontal lines in matching colours near -13 show the error without privatisation. The top plot uses unequal budget splits, labelled as (epsilon_p, epsilon_v) pairs from (0.02,2.00) to (2.00,0.02). Its curves form a U-shape: error is high at both extremes and lowest near the middle splits. The bottom plot uses equal splits with total budget falling from (1.00,1.00) to (0.10,0.10). Its curves rise as the budget shrinks. Blue sits above orange, and orange above green. The eye goes first to the blue curve's sharp rise at the right edge.
caption: Log average MSE, ln ¯E, for 20 (blue), 50 (orange), and 100 (green) data points on the sphere. Dotted line are the energies without privatisation. Top: unequal budget splits ϵp ∈[0.02, 2.0], ϵv ∈[2.0, 0.02], total ϵ = 2.02 and Bottom: Equal budget splits with varying total budget ϵ ∈[0.2, 2.0].
abstract: In statistical applications it has become increasingly common to encounter data structures that live on non-linear spaces such as manifolds. Classical linear regression, one of the most fundamental methodologies of statistical learning, captures the relationship between an independent variable and a response variable which both are assumed to live in Euclidean space. Thus, geodesic regression emerged as an extension where the response variable lives on a Riemannian manifold. The parameters of geodesic regression, as with linear regression, capture the relationship of sensitive data and hence one should consider the privacy protection practices of said parameters. We consider releasing Differentially Private (DP) parameters of geodesic regression via the K-Norm Gradient (KNG) mechanism for Riemannian manifolds. We derive theoretical bounds for the sensitivity of the parameters showing they are tied to their respective Jacobi fields and hence the curvature of the space. This corroborates, and extends, recent findings of differential privacy for the FrÃ©chet mean. We demonstrate the efficacy of our methodology on the sphere, $S_2\subset\mathbb{R}^3$, the space of symmetric positive definite matrices, and Kendall's planar shape space. Our methodology is general to any Riemannian manifold, and thus it is suitable for data in domains such as medical imaging and computer vision.
